subject: Next steps: RetainMed custom evaluation plan & scoring rubric
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@retainmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: RetainMed custom evaluation plan & scoring rubric

Hi Emma / Dr. Ortiz,

Thanks again for the call today — great to map the primary use cases and requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your custom eval running on Redwood: 

Recap (short):
- Goal: automated discharge summaries + follow-up message suggestions for care coordinators (priority: accuracy, no PHI leakage).
- Primary KPIs: factual accuracy, hallucination rate, average tokens/cost, and inference latency at 200-token responses.
- Data: you can provide anonymized historical cases (ideally ~2k rows) in CSV with the schema attached.

Redwood-recommended baseline models for the pilot:
- llama-70b-int8 (open-source, strong long-form fidelity) — recommended for model-fit runs where latency budget is higher.
- redwood-13b-q4 (Redwood-optimized 13B quant) — good tradeoff for latency/cost; useful to compare head-to-head.

Artifacts we attached/linked:
- retainmed_prompt_bank.md (prompt templates & edge-case probes) [Attachment]
- retainmed_sample_schema.csv (CSV schema example) [Attachment]
- redwood_eval_template.xlsx (scoring rubric + scorer instructions) [Attachment]
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid-retainmed-eval

Proposed evaluation design and timelines:
1) Dataset handoff: you upload anonymized CSV to the secure S3 bucket we provide (we can provision a short-lived upload link).
2) Pilot run (10 business days): we run model-fit tests across the two recommended variants, generate per-case outputs, and compute automated metrics (ROUGE/F1 where applicable, hallucination flags, response time).
3) Human scoring: we run a 500-case scorer pass using the attached rubric (inter-annotator agreement check included).
4) Review & recommendations: delivery of a results pack + model recommendation + cost/latency trade-off sheet.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Can you confirm the anonymization approach (PHI redaction vs. pseudonymization)?
- Are there any hard exclusions for training/eval (e.g., sensitive fields we must drop)?

Next immediate asks (if you can do these by Thu):
- Share a small sample (50 rows) using the CSV schema (retainmed_sample_schema.csv).
- Confirm legal/compliance contact for PHI questions (we'll loop in Security if needed).
- Confirm the preferred pilot window (we suggested Jul 5–16).

If that all sounds good I'll schedule a short kickoff with Ops and provision the upload link.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
[Attachment: retainmed_prompt_bank.md (text/markdown)]
[Attachment: retainmed_sample_schema.csv (text/csv)]

Subject: Re: Next steps: RetainMed custom evaluation plan & scoring rubric

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) PHI handling: our security team prefers pseudonymization for evaluation sets rather than full redaction so annotators can still judge context. We'll confirm the exact fields to pseudonymize but plan to remove direct identifiers (name, SSN).
2) Compliance: we are SOC2 Type II and will need to see the SOC2 report and data-handling notes from Redwood (or the private deployment options). Can you share that?
3) Sample: I'll try to get a 50-row sample by Wed EOD.

Also — curious about "hallucination flags" you mentioned. Are those automated heuristics or human-labeled?

Thanks,
Emma
Director of Product, RetainMed
emma.jones@retainmed.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: RetainMed custom evaluation plan & scoring rubric

Emma — quick answer on the hallucination checks: we use a two-layer approach.

1) Automated heuristics during inference: entity verification (does the output reference an entity not present in the input), contradiction detectors, and extraneous-fact matching against the input text. These are rule-based and give a binary flag per case.
2) Human QA pass: scorers mark hallucinations when the model asserts clinical facts that are not supported by the input or the source record. That is the ground truth for final reporting.

I've uploaded a short benchmark guide and the Redwood eval template to the shared Drive (linked below). The template includes suggested thresholds for initial acceptance (e.g., >92% factual accuracy on the scorer sample, <3% severe hallucination rate).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid-retainmed-eval

Attachment: redwood_eval_template.xlsx

Lauren — I'll coordinate with Ops to include the SOC2 artifact and a short note on our Private deployment data flow (we can do an encrypted S3 handoff or use your VPC Connect).

- Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@retainmed.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: RetainMed custom evaluation plan & scoring rubric

Hi all — operational note from the infra side on how we'll run the eval once you provide the sample dataset. I put concrete instructions below so your SRE/data-team can follow easily.

1) Dataset layout and upload
- Acceptable: CSV with columns: case_id, input_text, patient_age_range, encounter_date, gold_summary (optional). See attached retainmed_sample_schema.csv.
- Size: pilot can start with 50–500 rows; full scorer pass uses 500 rows.
- Upload: we will create a pre-signed S3 upload link for your team. After upload we validate schema and run a quick checksum.

2) Scoring criteria (automated + human) — included in redwood_eval_template.xlsx but excerpted here: 
- Factual accuracy (human scorer): 0–100 scale, target >= 92 for pilot acceptance.
- Hallucination rate (human severe): % of cases with a severe hallucination, target <= 3%.
- ROUGE-L (automated) for summary overlap; baseline reference included.
- Latency: p50 and p95 response time for a 200-token generation target; p95 target < 450ms on Dedicated; report observed.
- Cost: tokens-per-response and estimated per-1k cost for each model variant.

3) How we run the job on Redwood (CLI example)
- We will schedule runs via our eval runner. Example command (internal):
  redwood eval run \n    --model "redwood-13b-q4" \n    --input-s3 s3://redwood-uploads/retainmed/pilot.csv \n    --output-s3 s3://redwood-results/retainmed/pilot-20270623.csv \n    --prompt-bank retainmed_prompt_bank.md \n    --batch-size 8 \n    --metrics automated,hallucination

4) Security & compliance callouts
- SOC2 report: Ben will share the artifact.
- Data residency: your data stays in the bucket we provision; for Private deployments we can run entirely inside customer VPC.

5) Suggested timeline
- Wed Jun 23: we provision S3 link once sample confirmed.
- Jul 5–16: comparative runs + human scoring (if you prefer earlier, we can compress to 7 business days).
- Jul 19: results review call.

Please confirm: (A) you can provide a 50-row sample by Wed EOD, and (B) whether pseudonymization is acceptable (we will treat any uploaded data as PHI until we receive your compliance sign-off).

If yes, Ben and I will set up the kickoff and Ops will provision the upload link.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
